memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary but operationally separate ethics concerns. The reference frame focuses on equitable compensation across burden components and study circumstances, while the compared frame covers field-study safeguards involving mitigation, accessibility, privacy, equipment, withdrawal, non-retaliation, and overlooked workplace burdens.

relations.reason: These reference-side statements split one compensation principle into its budget basis, relevant time components, fairness rationale, and iterative-study application; the compared frame does not state a compensation rule.
relations.summary: Compensation should reflect total participation burden, including session, preparation, travel, and repeated-participation time.

relations.reason: This is a standalone reference-side payment-method policy with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: This reference-side rule concerns proposal-stage payment-method flexibility, which the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: A proposal need not finalize the payment method when compensation equity is adequately explained.

relations.reason: This is a distinct reference-side modality-equity rule without a compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Equal task burden should receive the same base hourly rate across face-to-face and remote studies.

relations.reason: This reference-side exception protects accrued compensation after study-caused disruption and is not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for time already invested when prototype errors terminate a session early.

relations.reason: This is a reference-side observation about a recurring calculation tendency, not a policy stated in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to omit between-session preparation burden from iterative-study compensation calculations.

relations.reason: The compared-side statements express the same task-level burden–mitigation correspondence through proposal documentation and reviewer verification; compensation is a different operational decision.
relations.summary: Each field-study task should have corresponding anticipated burdens and mitigation strategies that an ethics reviewer can verify.

relations.reason: These compared-side statements are complementary parts of one accessibility plan, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field studies should identify necessary accessibility accommodations and explain how they will be provided.

relations.reason: This compared-side data-handling safeguard has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately upon collection.

relations.reason: The compared-side statements split one equipment-loan plan into provision and return logistics, neither addressed by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Equipment lending should identify gear supplied to participants and define its return procedure.

relations.reason: The compared-side statements present the practical safeguard and its assessment rationale as one withdrawal-safety requirement, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field participation requires a safe alternative work procedure so withdrawal risk can be assessed and participants can resume existing work.

relations.reason: This compared-side non-retaliation protection is independently useful and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline participation should face no disadvantage in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: This compared-side observation identifies a field-study assessment tendency not described in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user tends to underestimate burdens from work interruption and exposure to a manager when sessions are short.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame requires task-level burden mitigation, accessibility planning, data separation, equipment logistics, safe withdrawal, and protection from workplace disadvantage, while noting underestimated interruption and managerial-exposure burdens.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame defines compensation around total participation burden, modality parity, payment flexibility, iterative participation, and disrupted sessions, while noting a tendency to omit between-session preparation.
